C-30.Name: Large-document open on WebKit: stop O(n²) block-lexer regex scans (sticky block rules)
C-30.IntentSummary: Make every non-global, non-multiline `^`-anchored muya block rule a sticky regex whose exec resets lastIndex to 0, so JavaScriptCore tries a match only at position 0 instead of scanning the remaining document after every block. Pin byte-identical lexer output with a golden token corpus captured before the edit, and gate the WebKit cost with a Playwright WebKit perf spec.

T-001.Title: W1: golden token corpus captured on the unmodified lexer

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: tests/renderer/muya/fixtures/lexer-corpus/ holds markdown inputs covering GFM tables (pipe and no-leading-pipe), nested and ordered lists, task lists, blockquotes (nested, lazy), every hr variant, setext and ATX headings, fences, indented code, front matter, footnotes, math blocks, html blocks, def links, plus a generated large document; each input has a golden JSON of Lexer.lex output produced BEFORE blockRules.js is touched.
lexer-token-parity.test.js compares Lexer.lex output to the goldens for both gfm and pedantic options and passes on the baseline code.

blockRules.js converts, after normal/gfm/pedantic are built, every RegExp rule whose source starts with `^` and whose flags have none of g/m/y into a sticky copy with an own exec that resets lastIndex to 0; non-RegExp, g/m and unanchored rules are untouched. File gains MODULE_CONTRACT, MODULE_MAP, START/END_BLOCK_STICKY_ANCHORED_RULES and CHANGE_SUMMARY.

block-rules-sticky.test.js: converted rules are sticky; two consecutive exec calls on different strings both match at index 0; String.prototype.replace through a converted rule (checkbox) behaves as before; `item` (gm) and other unconverted rules keep their flags.
Token parity test still green (byte-identical goldens).

tests/e2e/perf/large-doc-webkit.spec.ts opens a generated large document through the tauri shim in the WebKit engine, measures main-thread busy time with an in-page lag meter, asserts all headings rendered and busy time under the budget (6 s initial).

playwright.config.ts adds a `webkit-perf` project limited to tests/e2e/perf/**; the chromium project ignores tests/e2e/perf/** so the existing suite and CI chromium job are unchanged; package.json gains `test:e2e:perf`.
The spec fails on the pre-fix code (verified once by temporarily reverting W2 locally) and passes after it.

T-004.Title: W4: full gates, real-app measurement, governance

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Full vitest (coverage thresholds) and Chromium e2e green.
Real app re-measured on a local release build with the diagnosis bench (big.md, rich.md, 3 runs each); before/after recorded in the spec Completion evidence.
V-M-011 gains a scenario and commands for the parity test and the WebKit perf spec; graph M-011 notes the sticky block-rule invariant; CHANGE_SUMMARY entries present.

Review-1.Angle: correctness: sticky/anchor equivalence for every converted rule, lastIndex state leaks across exec/replace/match/split callers, corpus coverage of the five hot rules

Review-2.Angle: test and CI hygiene: perf budget flakiness, project isolation in playwright.config.ts, GRACE consistency
